basis: Tab. 4.1 'Energy and material need split for processing steps in jute mill', whole-mill figures split by the step shares; the yarn steps (opening/batching 20 %, carding 40 %, combing/flyer 10 %, spinning 10 %) are 80 % of the total. Per 1 kg of yarn.

items.name: electricity, low voltage, at grid
items.quote: Hessian for textile       18 %        ∅ 1250 MJ/t                  9.4 kg/t batching oil    Transport 250 km local
items.per: per kg of yarn produced from bast fibres
items.factor_source: 80 % of 1250 MJ per tonne, 1 t = 1000 kg, 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ -> 0.278 kWh/kg
items.note: The dataset's includedProcesses names exactly the steps opening, batching, carding, spinning, which Tab. 4.1 splits as 20 % + 40 % + 10 % + 10 % = 80 % of the mill's energy; the remaining 20 % is weaving, a separate dataset. The energy is 'electricity mainly'.

items.name: batching oil
items.quote: Hessian for textile       18 %        ∅ 1250 MJ/t                  9.4 kg/t batching oil    Transport 250 km local
items.per: per kg of yarn produced from bast fibres
items.note: '9.4 kg/t batching oil (petroleum based or vegetable oil as for example rice bran oil)' - the batching step belongs to yarn production, so the whole amount is allocated here.

items.name: transport, lorry
items.quote: Hessian for textile       18 %        ∅ 1250 MJ/t                  9.4 kg/t batching oil    Transport 250 km local
items.per: per kg of yarn produced from bast fibres
items.factor_source: 1 kg x 250 km = 0.001 t x 250 km = 0.25 tkm
items.note: 'Transport 250 km local trader to bast fibres mill (lorry)'; 1 kg over 250 km.

gaps: The report prints NO table for 'yarn production, bast fibres' itself; it appears only as a 1.16 kg input inside Tab. 4.2 (jute) and Tab. 4.3 (kenaf). Everything above is derived from Tab. 4.1 plus the step shares, so the amounts are indicative rather than read off.

Infrastructure is mentioned qualitatively - 'Infrastructure similar size and equipment than packaging plant', i.e. the 'packaging box production unit' module - but the excerpt gives no quantity for it, so no line is added.
No direct emissions: section 4.1.2 says explicitly 'No direct emissions were considered in the processing'.
Water, salt and auxiliary products are mentioned in 4.1.1 as inputs from the technosphere but no amounts are given for the yarn step.
The split between electricity and other energy carriers is not given; 'electricity mainly' is all that is stated.
